#termmax @termmax  前几天在 @termmax 体验了一把当债主，本打算舒舒服服吃个 9% 的年化利息。放出去的是硬通货 USDC，想着到期连本带利收回，妥妥的无脑理财。谁料借钱那哥们在第 25 天居然不还钱了！更离谱的是，系统直接往我地址里打了一堆 PT-sUSDe。原来这平台搞的是“以物抵债”（physical delivery），坏账了不负责卖货，直接把质押物强塞给资金方。

按以前在 Aave 或者 Compound 的经验，遇到烂账，清算机器人会立刻去竞价抛售。出资方拿回来的依然是稳定币，顶多承担 5% 的清算罚款。但在 TermMax 这里，压根没有竞价环节。这套玩法对那些没啥交易量、脱手极难的标的（比如 RWA 或 tokenized stock）确实管用。但这等于是把“套现难”的黑锅，从协议端完美转移到了咱们散户头上。

掏出计算器一敲，心都凉了。拿到那批 PT-sUSDe 时，盘面价已经跌破面值 1.8%。更要命的是，距离最终兑付还有足足 18 天。我去 DEX 瞄了一眼，池子浅得令人发指，稍微抛一点就会砸出 3% 的滑点！强行变现不仅白干，还要倒贴 Gas 费。但要是死等，这 18 天的空窗期里，万一 sUSDe 对应的底层协议出点幺蛾子，我连割肉跑路的机会都没有。

这波纯属用真金白银交了学费。以后去 TermMax 赚收益，千万别被利率蒙蔽双眼。掏钱前先扪心自问：如果对面爆仓了，你愿不愿意抱着他的资产过夜？如果不想，这单就别碰。这套交割机制对项目方来说确实是个 feature，但背后的流动性深坑，全凭咱们自己硬扛。#eth $ETH

title: Don't Just Do Your Research. Challenge It.
subTitle:
Doing research doesn't mean collecting information that supports what you already believe. That's confirmation bias. Real research should challenge your assumptions. If you believe a project has strong potential, ask:
🔹 What could make this project fail?
🔹 What are its biggest weaknesses?
🔹 Who are its strongest competitors?
🔹 Is the token actually necessary?
🔹 What happens if adoption doesn't grow?
🔹 What would make me change my mind?
The goal isn't to prove yourself right. The goal is to discover whether your thesis can survive serious questions.
🔑 Key Takeaway: Research that only confirms your belief isn't research. It's reassurance. A strong investment thesis should survive both the bull case and the bear case.
🧠 Practical Reflection; Before your next investment, write down two things: Why could this investment succeed Then ask: Why could I be completely wrong? If you cannot answer the second question, your research may not be finished.
Thought for the Day. Don't research to find reasons to buy. Research to discover whether buying actually makes sense.
Systems over emotion. Conviction over noise.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Earlier, in a coffee shop, I was chatting idly with a coworker. I thought I’d show off a bit about the underlying logic of blockchain—only for him to throw out a tricky question right away. Their company plans to move a chunk of institutional assets onto the chain. The bottom line is not only to satisfy official audit requirements, but also to prevent competitors from peeking at their cards. At that moment, I was completely stunned. In the crypto space, hasn’t the supposed “deal” between anonymity and compliance always been an unsolvable knot?

With a head full of doubts, I went to get a deep primer on <t-2/> Dusk Network, an L1 blockchain that focuses on financial confidentiality. After going through the materials, I found that the most core, hard-hitting weapon is the Phoenix UTXO architecture. You see, with Ethereum’s old-school account model, transfers are basically like running around in the nude—you can trace everything by following the trail. Dusk counters this with a one-two punch: Nullifiers (spent/obsolete markers) combined with a Merkle tree. I even walked through the testnet and tried contract deployment and payments. What I found was that it doesn’t expose the “thickness” of your wallet or who the recipient is. The system simply takes the amount you used to generate a dedicated hash and drops it into a nullifier pool, then packages the newly received funds into a new node on the Merkle tree.

I have to say, this stealth technique really has two moves. Outsiders can’t piece together the in-and-out flow of funds. With that, major institutions no longer have to worry about robots intercepting their positions while building their stakes.

But the problem spots are just as glaring.

After interacting with it myself, the side effects of this mechanism drove me crazy. Because every on-chain action requires generating a zero-knowledge proof locally and then validating the Nullifier, even though the project team specifically tinkered with Piecrust zkVM to speed things up, in real use those seconds of proving delay caused by client-side computation are unbearable for players who are used to near-instant, second-level responsiveness.

Personally, I think Dusk’s attempt to swallow the big pie of compliance-oriented privacy and real-world assets (RWA) is definitely a compelling story. But market survival never trades in fairy tales. With current policy directions being extremely strict, a “selective disclosure” chain can, with one misstep, trigger the risk controls of major firms and get forced offline. So here’s a heads-up for the project team: if you want the ecosystem to have a steady flow of users, don’t just obsess over lofty capital. #dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Last weekend, I met up with a friend for tea. I planned to discuss blockchain’s underlying layer with him—but this brother came back with a god-level request: their firm intends to move some assets on-chain, with the condition that they can’t just keep the doors open to the authorities, they also have to lock down transaction details so tightly competitors can’t get a thing. After hearing it, I was like, “Well, damn!” In the crypto world, isn’t anonymity and compliance supposed to be a case of no harm done to each other? 

With doubts in my mind, I did an in-depth investigation into Dusk Network, an L1 chain focused on financial privacy. After chewing through the materials, I found that the hardest-core ace up its sleeve is the Phoenix UTXO architecture. As everyone knows, Ethereum’s traditional account model is basically “running around in the nude” when you transfer funds. Dusk, on the other hand, uses Nullifier plus a Merkle tree mechanism. I ran it through the testnet and tried making payments and executing contracts. What’s impressive is that when you submit a transaction, it doesn’t expose your inputs or the recipient. The system simply takes the spent amount, generates an independent hash, throws it into a discard pool, and then turns the new funds into hidden nodes.

This logic really has something to it! Outsiders can’t figure out the upstream and downstream of the money flow, and big players finally don’t have to worry about their positions being front-run by machines.

But every story has a cost. In practice, the biggest pain point is: stuttering.

Because every time the state refreshes, it forces the local client to run zero-knowledge proofs and verify the Nullifier. Although the Dusk team has been tinkering with a dedicated Piecrust zkVM to speed things up, the few seconds of generation delay are still hard to ignore. Once you’re used to the smooth operations you normally get, sacrificing fluidity just to stay hidden really does hurt the experience.

Dusk wants to package the benefits of institutional-level RWA and compliant privacy—sounds tempting. But the market has never looked at technology alone. Now policy strings are getting tight; privacy chains built on “selective transparency” have a real risk of being taken down by mainstream platforms at any moment. Honestly, I’d advise Dusk one thing: take more care of regular retail users’ feelings, and don’t just keep staring at the giants. If no retail users are there to support the stage, even the sexiest vision will eventually turn cold.#eth $ETH

I can’t believe I took that silent loss—I just kept slapping my thigh in frustration! 

For the sake of stability, I went and looked into the project @TermMax. Honestly, the Range Order that TMX loudly claims to be its biggest feature does have something to it. The玩法 (mechanics) is quite similar to Uni V3’s concentrated liquidity. We can set conditions within our preferred APR range for automatic matching, and it even supports one-click looping with leverage. 

With a try-it-out mindset, I watched the charts and ran it for almost a month. The sweet spot of this system is that it lays out your profits clearly and cleanly. Back then I put in a bit of ETH, minted GT, then sold off FT in a handoff, and used it to borrow 2,000 USDC to place a trade with a 14-day cycle. The underlying model called TermMaxCurve is extremely forceful—it essentially locked my annualized return at 5.8%. Over the next few days, I felt at ease checking parameters and assembling parts in the workshop. I didn’t have to keep grabbing my phone every few days to check live quotes like I have some kind of obsessive-compulsive disorder. 

But there’s no such thing as a free lunch. Only after you wade into the water do you learn how deep the traps really go. Many people don’t realize that TermMax’s secondary order book is extremely weak right now—maybe the hype hasn’t caught up yet. A while back I needed money urgently, so I wanted to liquidate my FT early at a discount. What happened? Because of the AMM model combined with a sadly thin number of posted orders on the book, the trading slippage was absolutely outrageous, wiping out nearly 30% of my expected interest. When I saw the statement, I almost spewed out an old mouthful of blood. 

What really messes with your head is this: when you click that one-click leverage feature, the system’s underlying Router has to run several smart contracts back and forth. Each interaction burns Gas like crazy. For small retail folks like us who don’t have a huge principal, don’t touch it. 

All in all, TMX, by using FT, GT, and range order mechanisms, really does bring some new flavors to the fixed-income circle. But until market-making capital and liquidity gaps are filled, the cost of bailing out mid-way is just too brutal. Guys, if you’re planning to jump in, please—don’t go all-in at once! #eth $ETH

title: 活跃地址创7年新低，比特币为何死扛6.3万不破？
subTitle:
比特币活跃地址跌至54.5万个，创2018年以来最低纪录。但诡异的是，$BTC价格却在6.3万—6.5万美元区间稳如磐石。链上明明冷清得像熊市，价格为什么不跌？

这背后，是三个同时发生的"撤退信号"。

**第一重萎缩：用户活跃度回到7年前**

根据CryptoQuant数据，8月9日比特币活跃地址数降至545,233个，这是自2018年以来的最低读数。活跃地址（Active Addresses）指在24小时内发生转账的唯一地址数量，是衡量区块链真实用户参与度的核心指标。

如果把时间拉长，30日简单移动平均线从2025年10月的约72.2万个，一路下滑到8月初的约64.4万个，跌幅超过10%。换句话说，每天链上转账的"人头"少了将近8万个。

但价格呢？BTC从10月的12.5万美元跌到现在6.4万，跌幅接近50%，却在最近两周彻底"躺平"——63K到65K之间来回摩擦，振幅不到3%。散户参与度降到冰点，价格却没有继续崩盘。

**第二重萎缩：矿工也在"割肉"跑路**

截至8月15日，比特币矿工持仓降至约119.19万枚BTC，为今年5月31日以来的最低水平，单周减少885枚。矿工持仓（Miner Holdings）反映矿工钱包中未出售的比特币总量，是衡量矿工抛压的关键指标。

更值得关注的是Puell Multiple指标——当前值为0.75。Puell Multiple是矿工每日收入（美元计价）与365日平均收入的比值，0.75意味着矿工收入比过去一年平均水平低25%，处于历史上"利润承压但未绝望"的灰色地带。

这意味着什么？部分效率较低的矿机已经接近关机价，矿工被迫出售库存来覆盖运营成本。链上分析师监测到，疑似矿工的某个地址近20天累计向币安充值了6,494枚BTC，均价约6.48万美元——而一年前从机构平台收到这批币时，均价高达11.6万美元。跌了近一半，终于割肉。

**第三重萎缩：稳定币"干火药"持续缩水**

市场的弹药库也在收缩。自5月中旬以来，稳定币总市值从约3,220亿美元高点蒸发近150亿美元，目前维持在3,020亿美元左右。其中USDT市值从1,842亿跌至1,831亿，USDC从732.8亿跌至721.5亿，最近一个月两者合计缩水约22.3亿美元。

稳定币（Stablecoin）是加密市场的"现金等价物"，其供应量变化直接反映资金进出意愿。缩水意味着部分资金正在从加密生态回流法币，或者干脆离场观望。

三重萎缩叠加——用户跑了、矿工卖了、资金撤了——放在2022年，任何一条都能把BTC砸出10%的阴线。但2026年8月的市场，硬是在这种环境下横住了。

**价格不跌的真相：不是没人玩了，是玩法变了**

为什么？答案藏在三个结构性变化里。

第一，长期持有者（LTH）正在"锁死"供应。持有超过155天的地址占比已升至68.2%，创下历史新高。长期持有者比例越高，意味着市场上可交易的"浮动筹码"越少——即便散户活跃度下降，只要这部分"死多头"不松手，抛压就会被人为压缩。

第二，ETF机构化正在重塑资金通道。BTC现货ETF上周净流出约3.9亿美元，#ETH ETF却相对抗跌甚至小幅净流入。这说明机构资金不再主要通过链上钱包进出，而是通过传统券商的ETF通道配置。链上活跃度下降，未必等于市场关注度下降——只是"战场"从链上搬到了链下。

第三，巨鲸内部正在剧烈换手，而非单向抛售。CryptoQuant数据显示，巨鲸与散户差值指标在8月16日回升至0.407，巨鲸交易量中买入占比约47%、卖出约53%，整体趋于平衡。与此同时，10—10,000 BTC的中型巨鲸此前有明显的积累迹象。一边是老巨鲸派发，一边是新巨鲸接盘——筹码从"弱手"流向"强手"，这个过程本身不会引发价格暴跌。

**历史会重复吗？**

2018年7月，比特币活跃地址30日EMA约为57万个，到2019年1月升至60.5万个。随后BTC从3,000美元底部反弹至13,000美元。历史不保证重复，但"活跃度低谷+价格企稳"的组合，往往是市场情绪从恐慌过渡到麻木的标志性阶段。

当前的MVRV指标也提供了佐证。BTC整体MVRV约为1.22，意味着市场总市值是已实现市值的1.22倍——持有者整体仍在浮盈，但溢价率远低于牛市顶峰。更细分来看，持有6—12个月的"中期玩家"MVRV仅为0.64，说明这批在2025年底高位附近入场的投资者平均浮亏约36%。他们要是还没割肉，现在已经"麻木"了。

**结语**

54.5万个活跃地址、119万枚矿工持仓、3,020亿稳定币市值——三个数字都在告诉我们同一件事：链上世界正在经历一场"静默的出清"。但价格不跌，恰恰说明这场出清的接盘方，不是散户，而是愿意长期锁仓的机构和巨鲸。

对交易者来说，这比单纯的价格涨跌更值得警惕。因为当链上活跃度跌到这种程度，任何突发的增量资金涌入——无论是ETF逆转流入、还是宏观利好释放——都可能因为没有对手盘而触发剧烈的向上跳空。

你觉得这是"地量见地价"的底部信号，还是"流动性枯竭"前的暴风雨宁静？欢迎在评论区聊聊你的判断。

When I checked Dusk’s staking rules today, I only meant to confirm one thing: since the official website shows that more than 210 million DUSK are already participating in staking, can ordinary people simply deposit their coins and steadily earn returns?
After reading the official documentation, the answer isn’t that simple.
Direct staking has a minimum of 1,000 DUSK, and it doesn’t start counting immediately after you submit the transaction. New stakes only become eligible after the “next epoch boundary after the next epoch.” An epoch consists of 2,160 blocks; based on the target block time, normal activation typically takes about 6–12 hours. #ETH 
More importantly, direct staking corresponds to running a provisioner node. The node must stay online continuously, remain synchronized, be configured correctly, and use the required software version. Rewards depend on consensus participation and your effective staked amount relative to the network’s total effective stake. Therefore, it’s not a fixed-rate product—you can’t just extrapolate annual returns from a single day’s earnings.
The easiest detail to overlook is additional (top-up) staking.
After your original stake is activated, any additional amount only 90% becomes effective immediately, while the other 10% is recorded as locked stake. For example, if you add 4,000 DUSK, then 3,600 will immediately participate in consensus and 400 will go into the locked portion. The locked coins remain owned by the staker, but they do not participate in consensus. To retrieve that final portion, you may need to fully解除 (remove) the remaining positions.
Exit rules are actually more straightforward than I expected: once you successfully submit the transaction to解除 staking, the protocol itself has no waiting period. You can exit fully or partially, but the remaining position must still meet the 1,000 DUSK minimum threshold. However,解除 effective stake and locked stake do not automatically claim any previously accumulated rewards. Reward withdrawals still require a separate action.
These details change how I look at the “210 million DUSK already staked” figure. It does indicate that a large amount of tokens is participating in securing the network, but it can’t be directly equated with risk-free, fixed returns, or a savings-like investment you can deposit and withdraw on demand.

今天查 Dusk 的质押规则时，我原本只想确认一个问题：官网显示已有超过 2.1 亿枚 DUSK 参与质押，普通人是不是把币存进去就能稳定拿收益？
看完官方文档，答案并没有这么简单。
Dusk 的直接质押最低需要 1,000 DUSK，而且不是提交交易后马上开始计算。新质押要等到“下一个 epoch 边界之后的 epoch”才具备参与资格。一个 epoch 是 2,160 个区块，按目标出块时间计算，正常激活大约需要 6—12 小时。#ETH 
更关键的是，直接质押对应的是运行 provisioner 节点。节点需要持续在线、保持同步、配置正确，并使用要求的软件版本。奖励取决于共识参与情况以及自己的有效质押占全网有效质押的比例，因此它不是固定利率产品，也不能只拿某一天的收益外推全年回报。
我觉得最容易被忽略的是追加质押。
原有质押已经激活后，新追加数量只有 90% 会立即成为有效质押，另外 10% 会记为 locked stake。比如追加 4,000 DUSK，其中 3,600 枚立即参与共识，400 枚进入锁定部分。锁定的币仍归质押者所有，但不参与共识；要取回最后这部分，可能需要把剩余仓位全部解除。
退出规则反而比我预想得直接：成功提交解除质押交易后，协议本身没有等待期。可以全部退出，也可以部分退出，但留下的仓位仍需满足 1,000 DUSK 的最低门槛。不过，解除有效质押和锁定质押不会自动领取此前积累的奖励，奖励提现还要单独操作。
这几个细节改变了我看“2.1 亿枚 DUSK 已质押”这个数字的方式。它确实说明已有大量代币参与网络安全，但不能直接等同于无风险、固定收益或随存随取的理财规模。

quoteContent.body:
#termmax 
you know what i kept coming back to one thought while looking at @termmax  today.

Most projects launch the token first, then spend months trying to create reasons for people to care about it.

TermMax is taking the opposite route.

$TMX is set for TGE on August 25, but I’m looking at what already exists underneath it:

• 1.5M+ registered wallets
• 90K+ daily active users
• $90M+ TVL
• 10 EVM chains

I also found the liquidity side interesting. When funds aren't immediately matched, they can be routed through venues like Morpho, Aave, Venus and Pendle instead of just sitting idle.

But the part that actually made me stop was the fixed-rate model.

I’m used to DeFi money markets where rates move with utilization. TermMax lets lenders and borrowers agree on a rate for a specific maturity.

For me, that changes the question from “what’s the rate right now?” to “what rate am I locking in, and for how long?”....

Then there’s $TMX.

Through sTMX, the token is designed to connect back to protocol activity, with potential exposure to revenue generated from lending, trading and liquidation fees.

XP, AP and MP are also expected to become claimable around TGE, while the final distribution and lock details still matter.

But I’m deliberately not treating 1.5M+ wallets as automatic token demand.

Usage tells me people are using the product. It doesn’t tell me they’ll buy or hold $TMX.

That’s what I’ll be watching after August 25.

My question: can TermMax turn existing usage into lasting demand for $TMX?
#BTC

#termmax @termmax  At midnight, I dissected TMX (TermMax) ’s economic model piece by piece, and a set of core data raised my alarm: investors 28%, the core team 15%, and outside advisers 3%. This accounts for 46% of the quota—half the kingdom—and every single portion is locked up in a “small black room” for one year without exception. So, everyone has no choice but to turn a blind eye and tighten their grip on their pockets, or else move to control the pool through contracts. The big players are tied down to a single rope: one benefits, everyone benefits; one suffers, everyone suffers.

Think back to how the once-buzzing Sushiswap (SUSHI) fell from its throne. SUSHI originally released capital allocations in a stepped manner (half-year, one year, one and a half years). This timing gap directly wrecked the trust foundation: when the first tranche expired at the six-month mark, that group of people, desperate to cash out, dumped their tokens aggressively—crashing the token price through the floor—so those unlocking later could only cut their losses and exit. TMX learned this lesson and adopted a one-size-fits-all volume-release model. In essence, it forces everyone to sit at the negotiation table: either the whole group defends the price to raise market cap, or everyone pays the price together for assets to go to zero.

Once you understand the logic above, you realize the real money-printing machine is not in the current TGE (token generation event) stage that’s right in front of us. The most valuable strategic battleground is hidden in the vacuum period around the time one year runs out. Before the volume release (around month 11), the market will inevitably be shrouded in panic about “insiders about to dump,” and the token price will be severely undervalued. But if it transitions smoothly into month 13 and the board remains solid, then the “hanging bearish news” will transform into a massive upward engine. Therefore, precisely targeting the emotional mismatch between months 11 and 13 is the ultimate trading strategy.

At the end of the day, by putting up this kind of “lock 46% for one year” show, TMX indeed helps stabilize market sentiment. But anyone who has spent long enough in the crypto circle knows: whether TMX can truly survive both bull and bear markets doesn’t depend on how long it has been drawing big promises—it depends on whether, at that moment, there is anyone in the market willing to take over by paying real cash. By August 2027, whether the branded curator network, the institutional funding pool, and the RWA asset side can truly be brought to life will be the deciding factor between life and death. Understand the token model—don’t just do countdowns. Figuring out who the bag-holder is—that’s the real key. #eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax  深夜把 TMX (TermMax) 的经济模型拆解完，有一组核心数据引起了我的警觉：资方 28%、核心班底 15%、外脑顾问 3%。这占据半壁江山的 46% 额度，无一例外被关进为期一年的“小黑屋”。因此，各方为了保命，只能心照不宣地捂紧口袋，或者协议控盘。大户们被死死绑在了一根绳子上，一荣俱荣，一损俱损。

回想一下当年红极一时的 Sushiswap (SUSHI) 是怎么跌落神坛的。SUSHI 当初给资本的额度是阶梯式释放的（分半年、一年、一年半）。这种时间差直接摧毁了信任基础：半年到期的那波人，为了落袋为安疯狂派发筹码，直接将代币价格砸穿，导致后续解锁的人也只能割肉离场。TMX 吸取了这个教训，采取了一刀切的放量模式，其实质就是逼着所有人坐在谈判桌前：要么集体护盘做高市值，要么大家一起承受资产归零的代价。

理顺了上面的逻辑，我们就知道，真正的印钞机根本不在眼前的 TGE (代币首发) 阶段。最有价值的博弈空间，隐藏在一年期满前后的那段真空期。在放量前夕（第 11 个月左右），市场一定会被“内部人即将砸盘”的恐慌氛围笼罩，代币价格会被极度低估；但如果平稳过渡到了第 13 个月，盘面依然坚挺，那么“悬空利空落地”就会转化为巨大的上涨引擎。所以，精准狙击 11-13 个月这个时间段的情绪错配，才是最绝的交易策略。

归根结底，TMX 搞出这种“锁定 46% 一年”的阵仗，确实起到了稳定军心的作用。但咱们在币圈混久了都知道，TMX 能否真正穿越牛熊，不取决于它画了多久的大饼，而是到了那一刻，市场上有没有人愿意掏真金白银来接筹码。到 2027 年 8 月，其标榜的策展人网络、机构资金池以及 RWA 资产端能不能真正落地，才是决定生死的关键。看懂代币模型别只会倒计时，弄清楚接盘侠是谁才是硬道理。#eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax In the middle of the night, I tore apart TMX (TermMax)’s model and found a highly perplexing dataset: the institution has 28%, the team 15%, and the advisors 3%—totaling 46% of the core allocation, which is hard-locked for at least one year. On the surface, it’s packaged as “long-term building,” but seasoned players can see right through it—this is a deadlock where everyone restrains everyone else. Then, when the cliff period ends at month 12, a massive amount of tokens floods into the market all at once. If any of these big holders dares to cash out early, it will inevitably trigger a stampede, and in the end the token price will plunge. So the smartest move for the market makers is to stick together—either hold to death, or queue up to exit slowly.

Compare this setup with Sushiswap (SUSHI) back then, and the difference becomes obvious. At the time, SUSHI investors’ token allocations were released in batches (6 months, 1 year, and 1.5 years). That timing difference directly smashed the order book: once the 6-month tranche ended, the first profit-taking holders疯狂地 dumping and selling caused the token price to grind into the ground. Then, when the later unlockers saw the momentum was wrong, they had no choice but to sell along too. TMX, on the other hand, forces 46% of insiders to face the cliff unlock on the same day—effectively forcing big holders to form a unified front. Either they all pay to prop up the market cap, or they all hold hands and get wiped out.

If you follow the market makers’ game plan one step further, the real high-yield opportunity isn’t in the current TGE (token generation stage), but in the battle surrounding the cliff release. In the days leading up to the release (month 11), retail traders are filled with thoughts like “the whales will dump”—panic will drive the price deep into a hole. But once you make it past the release node (month 13), if the chart hasn’t collapsed, the market will stage a revenge rally where “bad news becomes good news.” Therefore, timing the expectation-based play in that window from month 11 to 13 is the high-odds strategy.

In the end, TMX’s “46% locked for one year” gimmick is meant to reassure everyone, but old investors know that a time-for-space scheme can’t change the essence: zero-cost tokens will be cashed out eventually. Whether TMX can survive the life-and-death ordeal doesn’t depend on how long it’s locked—it only depends on whether, on the day of the unlock, there’s real money on the other side stepping in to buy. If before August 2027 its claimed curator network, institutional funds, and RWA collateral can’t materialize, then it’s all just talk. Don’t just count down the days for your token research—figure out who the buy orders are on the unlock day. That’s the core. #eth $ETH

把这套路跟当年的 Sushiswap（SUSHI）一比，差距就出来了。当初 SUSHI 投资人的筹码是分批给的（半年、一年、一年半）。这种时间差直接把盘面搞崩：半年期一到，首批获利盘疯狂砸盘出货，直接把代币价格按在地上摩擦，后头解锁的人一看势头不对只能跟着抛售。反观 TMX，让 46% 的内部人在同一天面对悬崖解锁，等于是强行逼着大户们统一战线：要么一起出钱把市值托住，要么手拉手一起完蛋。

顺着庄家的算盘往下推，真正的暴利机会根本不在眼下的 TGE（发币阶段），而是悬崖释放前后的博弈。在释放前夕（第 11 个月），散户满脑子都是“大户要砸盘”，恐慌情绪会把价格砸出深坑。可一旦熬过释放节点（第 13 个月），如果盘面没崩，市场就会上演“利空落地即利好”的报复性拉升。因此，卡在第 11 到 13 个月这个窗口期去做预期博弈，才是高赔率的玩法。

说到底，TMX 搞“46%锁一年”的噱头给大家喂定心丸，但老韭菜都懂，这种时间换空间的套路，改变不了零成本筹码早晚要变现的本质。TMX 能否扛过生死劫，不看锁了多久，只看解禁那天有没有真金白银来接盘。如果在 2027 年 8 月前，它宣称的策展人网络、机构资金、RWA 抵押品不能落地，那全都是空谈。研究代币别光顾着倒数日子，摸清解禁那天对面的买单是谁，才是核心。#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  I’ve recently been studying compliance pathways for the privacy track, and Dusk’s design approach caught my attention. In order to integrate seamlessly with real-world financial systems, its underlying Phoenix model has specifically developed a “view key” function. The logic is straightforward: everyday transfers remain anonymous, but whenever an institutional audit occurs, it can retrieve data to assist the review. As HTX’s sharp assessment earlier put it, this is essentially a “licensed transparency.” From the perspective of commercial game theory, leaving a backdoor for regulators can indeed ease traditional funds’ concerns—this is also a core selling point supporting $DUSK ’s long-term narrative.

But if you dig deeper along this reasoning, you’ll find a critically fatal flaw: who exactly controls this “universal key” that can see through all on-chain data? The official solution is to establish a “regulatory committee” and control it jointly through multi-signature authorization. It sounds like power is distributed, but in the real physical world, multi-sig is far from resilient. Ultimately, whoever holds the key fragments is still ordinary natural persons living on common necessity—human beings. Humans have fixed residences, are subject to local laws, and their bank assets can be frozen. Faced with compulsory enforcement orders from a strong sovereign nation’s courts, this so-called “decentralization” that relies on individuals’ ability to withstand pressure would collapse instantly.

What’s most unsettling is that this committee is nearly invisible in the current materials. For an organization that holds the power of life and death over the system, what is its admission mechanism? Are its members intentionally distributed across different jurisdictions that are friendly to the crypto industry? If any key member faces legal coercion due to circumstances beyond their control, is there an on-chain mechanism for timely removal or hedging? Unfortunately, the whitepaper is conspicuously silent on this. Simply throwing out a professional term like “multi-sig management” as a shield cannot possibly fill such a massive trust vacuum.

For a privacy-flagged public chain, trust should be grounded in untamperable mathematics and code—not betting on the morals and real-life circumstances of a small number of people. If the rules for power handover remain forever opaque, then Dusk’s depicted compliance blueprint, to put it bluntly, is merely shifting centralized risk from the stage to the backstage. #eth $ETH

但顺着这个逻辑往下扒，你会发现一个极其致命的漏洞：这把能看穿全链数据的“万能钥匙”由谁来管？官方给出的解法是设立一个“监管委员会”，通过多重签名来共同控制。听起来权力被分散了，但实际上，多签机制在物理世界面前不堪一击。掌握私钥碎片的终究是一个个吃五谷杂粮的自然人。只要是人，就有固定的居住地、受制于当地的法律，名下还有冻结得掉的银行资产。面对强势主权国家法院的强制执行令，这种依赖个人抗压能力的所谓“去中心化”，瞬间就会土崩瓦解。

最让人感到不安的，是这个委员会在现有的资料中几乎处于隐形状态。一个掌握系统生死大权的组织，其准入机制是什么？成员是否刻意分散在对加密行业友好的不同司法辖区？如果某位核心成员遭遇不可抗力的法律胁迫，链上是否有及时的剔除或对冲机制？遗憾的是，目前的白皮书对此讳莫如深。仅仅甩出一个“多签管理”的专业术语作为挡箭牌，根本无法填补如此巨大的信任黑洞。

对于一个标榜隐私的公链而言，信任应该建立在无法篡改的数学和代码之上，而不是押注于少数人的道德感和现实处境。如果权力交接的规则始终不透明，那 Dusk 所描绘的合规蓝图，说难听点，不过是把中心化风险从台面上转移到了幕后。#eth $ETH

ETH is even stronger: up 18.34% to $2,293.85. XRP rises 17.51%, while BNB and SOL are also up roughly 6%–11% to start. Total market cap jumps about 7% in a day, reaching about $2.45 trillion. Key data: this has triggered at least the largest short liquidation since 2021—shorts are lifted away in a mass clearing. The Fear & Greed Index flips from “Fear” to “Greed” overnight.

- Short term: The liquidation wave itself is fuel. Short covering pushes prices higher, and the confirmation that $72,000 flips from resistance to support is crucial. The Fear & Greed Index turning around suggests there’s still fresh chase-long demand on the way, but leveraged long positions that chase highs are also starting to stack.
- Medium term: ETH’s 18% single-day gain shows this isn’t a BTC-only show—altcoins typically see more volume in these kinds of rallies, which is usually healthier than a single-coin spike. But if macro winds shift again, this high-leverage structure is just as prone to reverse and trigger liquidations.

My take
I’m bullish on direction, but you need to distinguish between “trend longs” and “chase-price longs.” As long as BTC holds above $72,000, the top of the six-week range (the former resistance zone) is the first support. If pullbacks don’t break it, the structure remains strong. ETH has greater elasticity—$2,293.85 isn’t the end point, but don’t expect 18% gains every day. Risk point: sentiment flips to greed overnight; after short-term overheating, a pullback can be very sharp. Liquidations are two-way.

Trump met behind closed doors with CEOs from the crypto and finance industries and is optimistic about the passage of the Clarity Act, with expectations for the regulatory framework taking shape heating up.

According to a report by The Block, Trump held a closed-door meeting in the White House Oval Office with a group of CEOs from both the crypto and finance sectors. After the meeting, sources familiar with the matter said Trump appeared "bullish" about the passage of the Clarity Act. The core of this bill can be summed up in one sentence: draw a clear line between whether crypto assets fall under the SEC or the CFTC, and clarify what counts as a security versus what counts as a commodity. In plain terms, it’s the "rule clarification" the industry has been calling for for years. Now the president himself is putting his name behind it and is even soliciting feedback. In terms of stance, it’s no longer about whether to regulate—it’s about how to regulate in a way that allows the industry to survive.

Market impact
- Short term: emotions get directly ignited. BTC is currently at $72,746.01 (24h +6.64%), ETH at $2,344.34 (+12.14%), and XRP is up even more, +25.36%. The expectation of regulatory easing is one of the narratives that capital recognizes most, and risk appetite in the near term is likely to keep rising.
- Medium term: if the Clarity Act truly becomes law, exchanges with higher compliance costs may actually benefit, and the final psychological barrier preventing U.S. institutional capital from entering would be removed. This is a structural positive, not a one-off pulse of news.

My take
I’m inclined to be bullish, but let’s be clear: the good news has already been partially priced in. From the $72,746 level upward, every step is already digesting expectations. A closed-door meeting does not equal passage of the bill—there’s still the hurdle of congressional voting in between. The risk of a pullback lies in the idea of "buy the expectation, sell the fact." ETH’s 12% rally suggests that funds are rotating into more elastic assets. In terms of positioning, holders can give the market time, but those without a position shouldn’t chase XRP up 25%—the cost-performance is the worst. The key is whether subsequent legislative scheduling updates can keep the momentum going.

translatedData.content:
I calculated TermMax’s borrowing fees and found that even a fixed interest rate can’t be read as simply as the number on the page.
Over the past couple of days, I’ve been studying TermMax. I originally had a very lazy understanding: whatever fixed interest rate the page shows, the borrowing cost is roughly that amount.
Last night I looked up the official transaction-fee formula and realized it’s not that straightforward. Besides the borrowing interest rate locked at execution, borrowing also involves GT minting fees and protocol trading fees. The numbers aren’t huge, but if you want to compare different platforms and only look at APR, your accounting will almost certainly be off.
I ran a sample calculation with a hypothetical order: borrow 2,400 USDT, set the matched interest rate at 7%, and there are 45 days until maturity. #ETH 
Using the parameters from the current official documentation: for stablecoin GT minting, the reference rate is 6%, the GT minting fee rate is 10%, and the borrowing fee rate is 3%. Plugging into the formula:
〔6%×10%＋7%×3%〕×45÷365×2,400
The result is approximately 2.40 FT.
Note that this 2.40 FT is not the total interest over 45 days; it’s only the transaction fee corresponding to this hypothetical borrowing. The borrowing itself’s fixed costs, execution slippage, the assets actually received, and the market price of FT when repaying early all still need to be considered separately.
I think there’s an easy-to-miss aspect of TermMax: what’s called “fixed” means the repayment ceiling under the worst-case scenario is locked in—it doesn’t mean the repayment path is completely locked. If later market interest rates rise, older FT may trade at a discount, and borrowers could buy FT in the market to repay, potentially lowering the real cost. Conversely, if liquidity is poor, it may not be worthwhile to handle the position early.

So when I look at the TermMax market going forward, I’ll first note four numbers: actual amount received, debt at maturity, remaining days, and transaction fees. Then I’ll look at LTV and the liquidation line. It’s a bit more work, but it’s far more reliable than rushing in just because of a nice-looking APY.
The 7% and 2,400 USDT above are just numbers I used to demonstrate the formula—they’re not current market quotes. The parameters may also change, so it’s best to re-check the official page before doing anything in practice. #termmax  @termmax

content:
我把 TermMax 的借款费算了一遍，发现固定利率也不能只看页面那行数字
这两天一直在看 TermMax，我原本有个很偷懒的理解：页面写多少固定利率，借款成本大概就是多少。
昨晚翻到官方的交易费公式，才发现事情没这么简单。除了成交时锁定的借款利率，借款还会涉及 GT 铸造和协议交易费。数字不算大，但如果要比较不同平台，只盯着 APR，账肯定会算歪。
我拿一笔假设订单试算了一下：借入 2,400 USDT，匹配利率按 7%，离到期还有45天。#ETH  
按照当前官方文档里的参数，稳定币 GT 铸造参考利率为6%，GT铸造费率10%，借款费率3%。套进公式：
〔6%×10%＋7%×3%〕×45÷365×2,400
结果大约是2.40 FT。
注意，这2.40 FT不是45天的全部利息，而是这笔假设借款对应的交易费。借款本身的固定成本、成交滑点、实际拿到手的资产，以及提前还款时FT的市场价格，还是要分开看。
我觉得 TermMax 有个容易被忽略的地方：所谓“固定”，锁住的是最坏情况下的还款上限，不代表还款路径被锁死。如果后来市场利率升高，旧 FT 可能折价，借款人可以去市场买FT还债，实际成本有机会下降；反过来，如果流动性差，想提前处理仓位也不一定划算。

所以我以后看 TermMax 市场，会先记四个数：实际到账、到期债务、剩余天数、交易费。然后再看 LTV 和清算线。这样虽然麻烦一点，但比看到一个漂亮 APY 就冲进去靠谱得多。
上面的7%和2,400 USDT只是我为了演示公式设的数字，不是当前市场报价。参数也可能调整，实际操作前最好重新核对官方页面。#termmax  @termmax

TermMax’s “high APY”—I suggest you don’t just look at the APY first.
When I first opened Dual Investment in Alpha (@termmax ), the APY really did catch my eye immediately. The numbers are right there, and it’s easy to think subconsciously: deposit, wait until maturity, and get interest.
But once I read through the settlement rules, I quickly erased the word “deposit” from my mind. It’s more like you received an upfront premium, while agreeing to buy someone’s tokens at a certain price—or to sell the tokens you hold.
Here’s a very straightforward example. Suppose I deposit 1,000 USDT, and the strike price I choose is $1. At maturity, if the token price is still above $1, I get back my USDT and the premium. The experience really does look like earning interest.
#ETH 
But if the token drops to $0.7, my 1,000 USDT would be converted into 1,000 tokens at the $1 strike price. The paper value would shrink to $700. The premium may still be received, but it might not be enough to cover the $300 unrealized loss.
It works the other way around too. If the party deposits tokens, and the price rises above the strike, the tokens could be exchanged for USDT at the agreed price. You get the profit, but the upside beyond that—if the price keeps climbing—may not have anything to do with you anymore.
So when I look at Dual Investment now, I don’t ask first “how high is the APY?” I ask myself two questions first: Am I willing to take tokens at this price? Am I willing to sell tokens at this price? If both answers are no, then even a high APY isn’t suitable for me.
There’s also an easy-to-overlook point: after the funds are used by the option buyer, exiting early doesn’t necessarily have liquidity on demand. Sometimes you need to wait for new capital to come in, or wait for the maturity settlement. This is absolutely not the same as a typical money-market or savings product with daily liquidity.
In the end, the gains from Dual Investment don’t appear out of thin air. What you receive is the premium; what you give up is part of the price option. I think it’s more reliable to check what assets you’d get back in the worst case first, and then look at the APY—this order makes more sense.
#termmax  @termmax

content:
TermMax这个“高APY”，我劝你先别只看APY
我刚打开 @termmax  Alpha里的Dual Investment时，第一眼确实被APY吸引了。数字摆在那里，很容易让人下意识觉得：存进去，等到期，拿利息。
但我把结算规则看完以后，马上把“存款”两个字从脑子里删掉了。它更像是你收了一笔权利金，同时答应在某个价格帮别人接币，或者卖掉手里的币。
举个很直白的例子。假设我存入1000 USDT，选择的行权价是1美元。到期时，如果代币价格还在1美元上方，我拿回USDT和权利金，体验看起来确实很像赚利息。#ETH  
可如果代币跌到0.7美元，我的1000 USDT会按1美元的行权价换成1000枚代币。账面市值只剩700美元，权利金虽然照拿，但未必盖得住这300美元浮亏。
反过来也一样。存入代币的一方，如果价格涨过行权价，代币可能按约定价格换成USDT。收益拿到了，但后面继续上涨的那段利润，也可能跟自己没关系了。
所以我现在看Dual Investment，不会先问“APY有多高”，而是先问自己两件事：这个价格我愿不愿意接币？这个价格我愿不愿意卖币？如果两个答案都是否，那APY再高也不适合我。
还有个容易忽略的地方：资金被期权买方使用后，提前退出不一定随时都有流动性，有时要等新资金进来，或者等到期结算。这跟活期理财完全不是一回事。
说到底，Dual Investment的收益不是凭空来的。你拿到的是权利金，交出去的是一部分价格选择权。先看最差情况下会拿回什么资产，再看APY，我觉得这个顺序更靠谱。#termmax  @termmax

It's late and I can’t sleep. The main reason is that today’s bullish candle is a bit something—so I can’t help but talk a little.

BTC went back above 72,000. ETH is even more dramatic: it jumped ten percentage points in a single day. SOL and BNB also moved along. A few days ago it was still the usual frustrating, low-volume grind. Overnight, the whole picture changed.

Honestly, this kind of market is more testing than a sideways range.

I looked over this week. The mood was already laid out early: it’s U.S. earnings season, and everyone is both cautious and afraid of missing out. The money hasn’t left—it’s just looking for the right pool. This move today, plain and simple, is a concentrated release of risk appetite. Whoever acts first sets the pace.

But the more like this, the more I need to pour myself a bucket of cold water: after a big surge, people who chase usually buy at the hottest emotional point. Then once a pullback comes, it’s the ones with heavier positions who panic first.

My approach right now is basically three sentences: If you already have a core position, don’t move it—when it rises too much, reduce bit by bit, and don’t be greedy for the last bite. If you don’t have a position, don’t chase the highs—wait until the first pullback doesn’t break down, and it’ll be no late to enter then. As for the contracts: after the big bullish candle, the wick spikes are the most brutal—reduce leverage first. Don’t let one spike wipe out a whole week’s profit.

I’m not trying to guess the top, but I also don’t plan to blindly add to my position when sentiment is at its hottest. How far this run can go still depends on whether volume can keep up.

Did you follow today, or are you still being honest and waiting for the pullback? Chat in the comments—let’s see how many of you held back like I did.

VanEck sets a $500,000 target for Bitcoin: not based on retail belief, but betting that governments will take the baton

VanEck has released a $500,000 Bitcoin target price for 2029. The core logic is the trend of reserve allocation by sovereign states and institutions.

This forecast isn’t a shot in the dark. The $500,000 figure corresponds to scenario assumptions about changes in the global financial system: sovereign wealth funds and government-level treasuries begin including BTC in reserve assets. Put simply, this is no longer a retail narrative—it’s a “government-level buy” narrative. If countries truly allocate even a small portion of their foreign-exchange reserves to BTC, the existing circulating supply would not be enough to absorb it, and the price would naturally be pushed up. Today, BTC is quoted at $72,786, up 5.95% in the past 24 hours, and market sentiment is clearly recovering.

Market impact
- Short term: The institutional target price itself acts as a sentiment catalyst. BTC’s 5.95% rise today, ETH up 9.19%, and XRP up 14.44%—the altcoin correlation suggests capital is accelerating into the market, not just a single coin moving.
- Medium term: If the “treasury reserves” narrative is endorsed by more sovereign institutions, Bitcoin’s pricing anchor could shift from a “risk asset” to a “reserve asset,” volatility would decline and the valuation center of gravity would move up. Conversely, if the narrative is disproven, $500,000 would be nothing more than a meaningless piece of paper.

My view
I’m bullish. The reason is simple: institutions daring to publicly post a 2029 timeline must be supported by positions and research reports—not just pump-and-dump rhetoric. If BTC can hold above $72,786, the next thing to watch is whether it can defend this level and form a new base platform. ETH ($2,319.89) leads among majors today, and the healthy rotation of funds is a good sign. The risk is that $500,000 is a four-year target—any macro tightening along the way could trigger a drawdown on the order of 30%. Holding through it is the key.

One-sentence translation: Institutions aren’t forecasting prices—they’re reserving a spot in advance for the “governments buying BTC” storyline.

ETH is now around 2326, moving while clinging to the recent high at 2359.

Honestly, this rebound is pretty healthy. In three days it rose from 1870 to above 2300—up more than 20%. The key is the money driving it: the spot market saw a net inflow over the past three hours, with all twelve candles being green. Large orders have kept coming in. The order book shows buy volume more than five times sell volume, and active trades are dominated by buyers. This isn’t a futures push upward—it’s spot buying with real money.

The news flow also matches. The ETF saw a single-day inflow of over $100 million, and institutions are picking up and accumulating.

But I won’t chase from this position.

Price has already ridden beyond the upper Bollinger Band; RSI is at 82—short-term is already overheated. What I’m paying attention to instead is this: as price moves up, the big-wallet long positions on the account side have actually dropped by almost 10% over the past seven hours. It looks like the whales are quietly reducing longs. The spot leverage long/short ratio has been pushed to 20:1—longs are extremely crowded. Funding rates are actually quite calm: over a day, positions rose 15%, and the funding rate is still sitting at 0.01%, which suggests longs haven’t yet paid the price. If there’s a pullback, the sell pressure to lock in unrealized profits won’t be small.

My bias is still moderately bullish on the trend, and I won’t deny that. The ETF is consolidating, spot is still buying, and the lows are getting higher one after another—structure hasn’t broken.

But price always moves faster than logic. If you chase at this point, you’re buying the trend for sure—but you’re buying at a spot that’s too hot. I’d rather wait for a pullback: come back to around the 2250 platform, or let it digest sideways for a few days, then see if it holds. Chasing highs isn’t my choice—confirmation after a pullback is.

How to Use the $ETH/$BTC  Ratio to Judge Rotation, Instead of Fixating on Absolute Price

Many people only look at how much ETH has risen or fallen. In fact, when configuring inside the crypto market, “the ratio contains more information than the absolute price.”

◆ What the Ratio Tells You
ETH/BTC reflects market preference for capital between two major assets.
- Ratio rising: capital is willing to take higher risk, often accompanied by the start of an altseason
- Ratio falling: capital moves into $BTC  collapse, and risk-off sentiment dominates, so altcoins are generally weaker

So when you look at the ratio, you’re essentially tracking the market’s risk appetite direction—not simply whether prices are going up or down.

◆ Three Practical Ways to Judge
1. “The ratio makes a new low, but ETH’s absolute price hasn’t broken its previous low” — This indicates BTC is too strong rather than ETH being too weak; the nature is completely different
2. “The ratio has been ranging in the historical low zone for months” — In history, this phase often corresponds to a window for long-term positioning, but “low” can last a very long time; don’t expect an immediate reversal
3. “The ratio surges with rising volume” — Usually a sign of capital flowing out of BTC; altcoin moves often start later

◆ Factors That Affect the Ratio
- How much of expectations for Ethereum network upgrades has already been priced in (good news landing often marks a stage top)
- Differences in capital inflows to spot ETFs
- Staking yields and on-chain activity

◆ A Reminder
The ratio is a relative indicator and cannot be used alone as a buy/sell signal. When ETH/BTC falls, both may be dropping—only the magnitude differs. A “better-looking” ratio doesn’t automatically mean you’ll make money.

Position management always comes before directional judgment. The above is my personal framework and does not constitute investment advice.

怎么用 $ETH/$BTC 比值判断轮动，而不是盯绝对价格

很多人只看 ETH 涨了多少跌了多少，其实在币圈内部做配置，「比值比绝对价格更有信息量」。

◆ 比值告诉你什么
ETH/BTC 这个数字反映的是资金在两个主流资产之间的偏好。
- 比值上行：资金愿意承担更高风险，通常伴随山寨季启动
- 比值下行：资金往 $BTC collapse，避险情绪占上风，山寨普遍更弱

所以看比值，本质是在看「市场的风险偏好方向」，而不是单纯的涨跌。

◆ 三个实用判断
1. 「比值创新低但 ETH 绝对价格没破前低」 —— 说明是 BTC 太强而非 ETH 太弱，性质完全不同
2. 「比值在历史低位区震荡数月」 —— 历史上这种阶段往往对应中长期布局窗口，但"低位"会持续很久，别指望马上反转
3. 「比值放量拉升」 —— 通常是资金从 BTC 外溢的信号，山寨行情往往滞后启动

◆ 影响比值的几个因素
- 以太坊网络升级的预期兑现程度（利好落地往往就是阶段性顶）
- 现货 ETF 的资金流入差异
- 质押收益率与链上活跃度

◆ 一个提醒
比值是相对指标，不能单独当买卖信号。ETH/BTC 走低时两个可能都在跌，只是跌幅不同——比值好看不等于你赚钱。

仓位管理永远排在方向判断前面。以上是个人框架，不构成投资建议。

#termmax @termmax To put money into fixed-income assets is easy; what’s hard is how to get out in the middle. Recently, while reviewing the TermMax 2026 whitepaper and its V2 architecture, I found that the Smart Unwind mechanism isn’t just about adding a redemption button—it fundamentally breaks the “rigid” label that fixed-income assets have long carried. In the underlying design, FT is responsible for paying out the fixed face value at maturity, while XT carries the corresponding interest obligations. In effect, it forcefully imprints the debt cycle into the token.

Looking back at V1, once a loan is finalized, the collateral and capital basically become “frozen ground,” and you can only hold hard until maturity is reached. But V2’s Smart Unwind opens a new line of thinking: it allows you to predefine the APR threshold you can accept or specific price conditions. Once the market reaches those conditions, arbitrageurs or new borrowers will take over the position. After this kind of shuffling, the collateral assets that were previously dormant are instantly activated, able to flow back into the market for renewed use.

Dig deeper, and it’s really breaking the biggest curse in the fixed-income circle: the assumption that agreeing on a maturity date means the position must stay locked until then. That’s not necessarily true. However, reality is always harsh. If you want to exit early, the prerequisite is that someone in the market is willing to buy in—and in practice, there’s often a significant gap between your target price and the prevailing market price. Whether this feature can truly boost capital turnover ultimately depends on real buy-side demand; you can’t make it work with mechanism code alone.

So going forward, I’ll closely monitor a few core metrics: first, the real probability of execution after orders are placed; second, the actual slippage users experience when the mechanism is triggered; third, how many times the same collateral can be reused before maturity. As long as these data keep trending positively, we can confidently say that TermMax V2 fundamentally overturns how fixed-term capital is operated—not merely by adding a new feature.#eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax Let’s talk about fixed-term lending and borrowing. The bottleneck in this business has never been lending out the funds—it’s what happens after the capital has been handed over: when you suddenly need money halfway through, how do you get out (“unwind”) the position. By carefully comparing TermMax’s 2026 whitepaper with its V2 version, I’ve noticed that Smart Unwind is far more than just adding a closing button; in practice, it dismantles the inherent “rigidity” of fixed-income assets.

Everyone knows that in the protocol, FT stands in for the maturity face value safety net, while XT carries the burden of paying interest—effectively locking the time horizon directly into the token’s underlying design. In the V1 stage, once the contract is live, the underlying collateral and the position become fossilized; you can only endure and wait.

But in V2, Smart Unwind gives you the initiative. It allows you to pre-list an expected APR or set a trigger price. Once the market hits your trigger, an arbitrage crowd with sharp instincts—or new borrowers entering the market—can directly take over your position. This “change of defense” frees the collateral that was previously confined, returning it to an actively usable state.

This design breaks a common assumption: a fixed term doesn’t mean the position must stay stuck in place.

However, we have to ground the discussion in reality: the cost of withdrawing early is very concrete. If you want to leave, there must be capital willing to take over; and often there’s a significant gap between your ideal exit price and the actual real-world price in the secondary market. Whether Smart Unwind can truly reactivate capital flow fundamentally depends on the support of genuine buyer demand—not merely a few lines of smart contract code.

Is this setup more than just a gimmick? Next, I’ll focus on three key feedback points only: 
1) Real turnover rate: if you pre-place an order to exit early, how likely is it that the trade will truly execute?
2) Real slippage: when the handoff is triggered, how painful are the friction costs created on the books?
3) Turnover frequency: for the same piece of collateral, before maturity, how many times can it be reactivated in practice?

If these on-chain metrics can steadily trend upward, then TermMax V2 can be considered as fundamentally reshaping the turnover logic of fixed-income capital. Otherwise, at best it’s just a nice-to-have ornament. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Dusk team recently had an insight into the fine print: don’t assume that once real-world assets are tokenized and put on-chain, buyers will automatically show up in the order book. That said, while the point is valid, I think taking this standard and using it to pressure their own underlying fundamentals is basically tailor-made.

To be fair, the cards they’ve been showing are indeed quite solid. Look at this lineup of partners: NPEX, the regulator of securities; 21X, which holds the European Reuters feed; Quantoz, which issues euro stablecoins; Cordial, which manages the funds pool; and Chainlink, which provides data infrastructure.

If you look only at the accounting ledger, the confirmed order book of €300 million, over 50,000 investment customers, and the more-than-200 million $DUSK tokens locked across the network—this combination of real and supposed activity does look very convincing.

But after watching the market for a long time, the biggest fear is only looking at “face-projects.” For traders, we care only about the real game of cash moving hands. Of all those assets entering under compliance banners, how many trades are actually completed on-chain with genuine turnover? As for the euro stablecoin Quantoz supposedly brought in—has it really been circulating in this space? And since it integrates with Chainlink interfaces, is any fresh external capital actually bridging over across chains? Remember, narratives can be flashy, but on-chain retention and Gas usage can’t be faked.

There’s a particularly stark contradiction here. If you check the applications they prominently promote, the only things you can actually use are super barebones infrastructure like Pieswap and Dusk Domains. On one side, you’ve got PR releases about institutional cooperation flying everywhere; on the other, retail users can’t even find a decent pool to farm for depth. The big-money liquidity is put up top as a display sign, while retail users below have no tools to use—this kind of gap is deadly.

So I have one guiding principle: I’m not bearish, but I need to see the rabbit before I start throwing the hawk. Everyone has already become numb to all kinds of “major partnerships.” The next lifeline is whether these glossy B2B protocols can turn into real TVL and daily active usage that retail can actually play. If the official side understands that putting assets on-chain doesn’t mean there is real water behind them, then going forward, stop pushing slogans—show the real buyers and the actual liquidity.

What’s amusing, though, is that if you use this same ruler to measure their own ecosystem’s current situation, it turns out to be almost exactly the same—down to the last detail.

Objectively speaking, the resources they currently hold do have real strength. Look at their lineup: NPEX, which focuses on compliant securities; 21X, which holds a Europe-wide passport; Quantoz, which issues euro stablecoins; Cordial, which leads in asset management; and Chainlink, which provides price feeds. If you only go by the books, a confirmed issuance of 300 million euros, more than 50,000 investment participants, and an additional 200 million-plus $DUSK  staked amount claimed across the network—this presence really does look quite impressive.

But as someone who has been watching the market for years, what I’m most wary of is this kind of “paper wealth.” I care much more about real, bottom-layer interactions of tokens and positions. With all this massive compliant-asset entry, how many deals are actually executed end-to-end on-chain with real settlement? That euro stablecoin Quantoz issued—has it actually been moving within the pools, or is it just on paper? And once they managed to connect to Chainlink, did they truly bring in fresh capital from outside the ecosystem? Remember: concepts can be hyped as much as you want, but blockchain data that’s stored on-chain can’t be faked.

What this reveals is an extremely absurd disconnect: when you go experience the on-chain ecosystem that DUSK strongly pushes, what shows up is still early and rudimentary stuff like Pieswap and Dusk Domains. It’s like this: B-side institutional good news floods in, but when it comes to letting C-side retail users actually come in and fight for real—plus providing deep, functional venues—there are only a handful. Institutional money is erected up on top like statues, while retail has nothing much to do at the bottom. The two sides are completely out of sync.

So my current bottom line is this: I won’t blindly turn bearish, but I also won’t jump on the bandwagon just because everyone says good things. #dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Dusk Foundation 官方近期吐露了一句大实话：千万别以为把传统资产包装上链，就能凭空催生出接盘侠和交易量。这话挑不出毛病。但逗乐的是，要是拿这把尺子去量一量他们自家的生态现状，可谓是分毫不差。

客观来说，他们目前攥在手里的资源确实能打。你瞅瞅这套班底：主做合规证券的 NPEX，揣着欧洲通行证的 21X，发行欧元稳定币的 Quantoz，主导资管的 Cordial，外加提供喂价的 Chainlink。如果单凭账本说话，3亿欧元的确认发行、5万多名投资客，再叠加上全网押着的 2亿多枚 $DUSK 质押额，这排场摆得确实足够大。

不过作为盯盘多年的老手，我最防备的就是这种“纸面富贵”，我更在乎筹码在底层的真实交锋。这么庞大的合规资产入局，究竟有几单是在链上真正跑通了交割？Quantoz 搞出的那个欧元稳定币，在池子里到底转没转起来？既然打通了 Chainlink 的桥，到底有没有把圈外的新鲜资金引进来？记住，概念可以随便吹，但链上的数据留存是装不出来的。

这其中暴露了个极其荒谬的断层：当你去体验DUSK强推的链上生态时，冒出来的居然还是 Pieswap、Dusk Domains 这种极其简陋的早期玩意。这就相当于，B端的机构利好铺天盖地，但真正能让C端老哥们下场搏杀、提供深度的场地，却屈指可数。机构资金在上层当雕像，散户在下层无戏可唱，两头完全是脱节的。

所以，我目前的底线是：绝不盲目看空，但也绝不见风就是雨。市场对那些“重磅合作”的公关稿早就不感冒了，接下来的生死局，就看这些光环能砸出多少真实的TVL和活跃度。既然你们也懂资产上链不等于自带活水，那以后就少来虚的，把真实的流动性摆到台面上来。#eth  $ETH

To be honest, yesterday’s big bullish candle line had me staring at the candlestick chart until late at night. Today, the first thing I look at isn’t the price—it’s the volume. After the move up, the volume is much more honest than the price: expanding volume continuing the assault is genuinely strong; contracting volume grinding around is mostly the old script—pull up, take a break.

Now BTC is hovering around 73,000, and ETH is holding its gains. Honestly, I’m not in a hurry to reach a conclusion. At this kind of position, the direction doesn’t matter that much—the key is how it treats 72,000. If it holds and stays above, that’s confirmation for yesterday’s move; if it turns back and breaks through 72,000, then don’t kid yourself—get out first and then talk.

Let’s also talk about mindset. For anyone who didn’t get in yesterday, today is the most painful—chasing means you’re afraid you’ll buy at the top, not chasing means you’re afraid it’ll fly even higher. My clumsy method: split my position into two parts—one waits for a pullback to enter, and the other stays ready for when there’s a real breakout. If the entry isn’t good enough, don’t force the buy. Money in your hand doesn’t burn you for a minute.

This ETH move has more elasticity than BTC. It’s more fun when it’s pumping, and when it pulls back it’s also more jumpy—so for my own allocation, I tilt the position size toward ETH. Also, this week the US stock earnings are coming in a string—Google, Tesla, you name it. Risk appetite can change on a dime. Don’t put all your bets on when the emotions are at their hottest.

What are you doing today? Taking profit, holding on, or waiting for a pullback? Leave a comment in the comment section—I’ll see who’s as much of a slowpoke as I am.

The most dangerous emotion today isn’t fear—it’s greed mixed with complacency. Up 5% and you think you were right, forgetting how much you lost last week. That’s what discipline is for—not to stop you from making money, but to keep you from adding to positions at the wrong time.

subTitle:
A Ilusão da Liquidez Sutil: Como o Retorno do QE Global Prepara o Maior Choque Monetário da História

​Nas sombras dos relatórios do Federal Reserve e das decisões de política monetária das autoridades globais, uma engrenagem gigantesca voltou a girar com força total. Longe dos holofotes do grande público e sob o disfarce de "ajustes operacionais", os Estados Unidos e os principais bancos centrais do Ocidente estão executando o que promete ser a maior expansão de liquidez da história moderna. Desta vez, porém, o motor não é a reestruturação do sistema bancário tradicional, mas a injeção sutil e contínua de capital que alimenta o ecossistema das moedas digitais e o apetite por ativos de risco em plataformas como a Binance.

​A Sutil Troca de Dívidas de Longo Prazo por Liquidez Imediata

​Durante anos, economistas defenderam que o dólar enfrentaria seu fim iminente devido ao descolamento entre a dívida pública norte-americana e a produção real. O que poucos previam era a extrema sofisticação com que a engenharia financeira atual operaria a rolagem dessa dívida.

​A "impressão" moderna de dinheiro não é feita com caminhões de notas físicas sendo descarregados na economia real. Trata-se de uma injeção cirúrgica de liquidez via mercados monetários e facilidades de crédito que contornam os canais tradicionais. Títulos públicos de prazos extremamente longos — com maturidades de 30 a 40 anos — estão sendo sutil e indiretamente liquidados.

​Em uma troca sutil, a dívida pública de longo prazo é colateralizada e convertida em capital especulativo imediato por meio de derivativos e stablecoins. A promessa de pagamento em quatro décadas transforma-se em poder de compra em questão de segundos.

​O Papel da Binance e das Criptomoedas na Absorção do Fluxo

​A Binance e as maiores corretoras mundiais tornaram-se os reservatórios perfeitos para essa massa monetária. Quando o Federal Reserve injeta liquidez nos mercados para estabilizar a dívida dos EUA, a busca por proteção contra a desvalorização fiduciária direciona esse capital diretamente para o mercado de criptoativos.

​O fluxo ocorre de forma direta:

​Injeção de Liquidez: Os bancos centrais expandem o balanço para rolar a dívida pública.
​Transformação em Stablecoins: A liquidez em dólares migra para tokens digitais atrelados à moeda americana.
​Entrada na Binance: As corretoras globais registram volumes recordes de negociação em um punhado de moedas estratégicas.

​Esse processo gera uma expansão monetária indireta que alimenta três pilares fundamentais do ecossistema cripto:

​Bitcoin $BTC : Atua como a reserva de valor suprema para onde o capital institucional foge quando percebe a diluição das moedas estatais.
​Ethereum $ETH : A infraestrutura base para os contratos inteligentes e liquidação automatizada de capital.
​Binance Coin $BNB : O combustível direto do maior ecossistema de liquidez do mundo, funcionando como termômetro da atividade especulativa global.

​Maior que Qualquer Quantitative Easing do Passado

​O ambiente que se desenha não tem precedentes. Os programas de Quantitative Easing (QE) implementados durante a crise financeira de 2008 e durante a pandemia de 2020 parecem ensaios tímidos perto do volume exigido para rolar a dívida global atual.

[QE 2008: US$ 1,5 Tri] ➔ [QE 2020: US$ 3,0 Tri] ➔ [Liquidez Atual: Sem Teto Teórico]

Diferente das fases anteriores do QE, o ciclo atual enfrenta três fatores sem precedentes:

​Digitalização Completa: A velocidade do dinheiro dobrou com o uso de stablecoins e plataformas de negociação 24/7.
​Pressão Fiscal Estrutural: O custo para rolar os juros da dívida dos EUA exige uma criação de moeda que supera o crescimento do PIB.
​Globalização da Liquidez: O capital vaza instantaneamente dos bancos de Wall Street para plataformas globais de negociação.

​O que estamos testemunhando não é uma simples reação a uma crise temporária, mas a reconfiguração definitiva do sistema monetário. A conversão de dívidas de 40 anos em liquidez digital imediata abriu as portas para uma expansão sem paralelo histórico — e o mercado cripto é o primeiro a registrar o impacto dessa nova era.

$ETH  Now 2311, it pulled back fifty dollars after sticking to the high of yesterday at 2359. In the past 24 hours, it was only hanging at less than two points; just a couple of days ago it was still 1905, and it got shoved up more than 20% in one go.

I acknowledge this round of money. For the spot market, in three hours, none of the 12 candles went into the red; net inflow is over 600k u. The ETF custodian is still moving money in, and the on-chain borrowed coins are up by half—real funds have come through.

But once it gets pushed to this level, the “smell” starts to be off. Retail accounts have 70% positioned long; the global long/short ratio is topping out at 2.2. Funding rate is still positive, and longs are squeezing in with a premium. However, the whale accounts’ long ratio is trending downward. The contract side’s active buy orders have shrunk to 47% and are still falling; in the last 15 minutes, large orders saw net outflows. The money used to push it up—someone is actively pulling it back out.

In plain terms: there are both inflows and outflows. Next, we just need to see whether the money keeps coming or not. Sentiment is above 8/10. Outside, the shouts are dragging on like the bull market has landed—this move has risen too fast at this point, and there’s a huge amount of floating profit.

I’m not chasing. This isn’t bearishness; it’s just that at this level, chasing longs has mediocre cost-effectiveness. I’ll wait for it to retrace and wash out the floating profits first. That’s how it ends up being.

BTC is currently trading at $72,640, up +4.34% in the past 24 hours. ETH is currently trading at $2,314, up +1.68% in the past 24 hours.

━━━ Regime Assessment ━━━
The Van Tian system shows that BTC is currently in the BEAR_RECOVERY regime, while ETH is in CHOP_MID. In other words—BTC is struggling to climb out of the pit, and ETH is still rolling around in the mud. These two words are the most important: RECOVERY, not BULL. In a bear market, rebounds have force, but they don’t have conviction.

━━━ Trading Mindset ━━━
When it’s up 4%, your greed starts to wake up. You begin to fantasize, “This time is different.” But I’ve seen too many of these markets: it’s precisely when emotions are at their loosest that you should tighten discipline the most. The market never rewards people who follow their feelings.

━━━ Strategy Direction ━━━
Under the BEAR_RECOVERY regime, if you go long, keep your position light and wait for pullback confirmation. Don’t chase—wait for the structure. ETH’s CHOP isn’t suitable for grid trading; wait for a directional breakout before saying anything. The right positioning for today should have been set up yesterday.
